deep.reconstruction:
Setting: X is an arbitrary topological space. Y ⊂ X is a 'non-singular' subspace, meaning a topological manifold.

(1) Equisingularity. X is called 'equisingular along Y' if for every y ∈ Y there exist:
- a pointed space (N,a),
- an open neighbourhood U of y in X,
- a homeomorphism U ≅ N × Y_U, where Y_U = Y ∩ U.
The homeomorphism must restrict on Y_U to the canonical map Y_U → {a} × Y_U. In modern terms, the pair (X,Y) is locally topologically trivial along Y: a topological 'normal slice' N times the stratum.

(2) Immobile points. A point x ∈ X is an 'elementary' or 'immobile' singularity if every manifold Y ∋ x along which X is equisingular has dim_x Y = 0.

(3) Mobility. A point x is ν-mobile if there exists such a Y with dim_x Y ≥ ν. One may then take dim Y = ν by passing to a coordinate sub-disc of Y. The 'order of mobility' of x is ν if x is ν-mobile but not (ν+1)-mobile. Immobile points are exactly those of order 0.

(4) Existence of ν(x). If X is locally finite-dimensional, every x has an order of mobility ν(x). It equals the sup of the dimensions of manifold germs through x along which X is equisingular. That sup is bounded by the local dimension, so it is attained.

What this serves (next page): the filtration Mob^i(X) = {ν ≥ i} and its complements F_i, giving a candidate canonical, purely topological stratification of X by 'mobility'. Grothendieck then asks three questions:
- Prop A: each stratum ν^{-1}(i) is a manifold and X is equisingular along it.
- Prop B: locally (X,Y_i) ≅ Y_i × (N,o), with o an immobile point of N, and the local type of (N,o) constant on components.
- Prop C: the stratum germ is the largest equisingular submanifold germ; the other such germs correspond to submanifold germs of Y_i.

In margins he calls spaces satisfying A 'presque raisonnables' and conjectures B for 'dévissable' spaces. This is the intrinsic (coarsest) topological stratification, conceived within his programme of 'topologie modérée'.
errors: Monotonicity issue for (4): bounding dim Y by the local dimension of X uses monotonicity of covering dimension for subspaces. This holds for metrizable or separable spaces but not for arbitrary topological spaces, so a mild hypothesis is implicit.

The N.B. (one can take dim Y = ν) and the later Prop C implicitly use that X stays equisingular along locally flat sub-submanifolds of Y. That is true, since R^k = R^{k-j} × R^j can be absorbed into N. It fails, or at least is unclear, for wildly embedded submanifolds of Y, which is presumably why Prop C speaks of 'sous-variétés régulières'.
Next page, Prop A: the stratum ν^{-1}(i) should have DIMENSION i, not codimension i. For X a manifold of dimension n, every point has mobility n.

In general Prop A can fail. Points of a given mobility can accumulate from outside a×Y_U, and ν^{-1}(i) need not be locally closed. Grothendieck acknowledges this by isolating the class of 'presque raisonnables' spaces.

ideas.what: Topological equisingularity of X along a submanifold Y: local homeomorphism U ≅ N × (Y∩U) compatible with Y ↦ {a}×Y
ideas.modern_name: Local topological triviality along a stratum / local cone-like (CS-set) condition
ideas.usually_credited_to: Thom, Mather (topological triviality); Zariski (word 'equisingularity', algebraic setting); Siebenmann (CS-sets, 1972)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5 discusses tame/stratified structures informally, without this definition

ideas.what: Order of mobility ν(x): max dimension of a manifold germ through x along which X is equisingular; immobile points have ν = 0
ideas.modern_name: Dimension of the intrinsic stratum through x (intrinsic/canonical stratification)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Goresky–MacPherson (Intersection Homology II, 1983), H. King (1985), Sullivan / Handel for related notions

ideas.what: Filtration Mob^i(X) and questions A/B/C: strata are manifolds, local product with an immobile normal slice, maximality of the stratum germ
ideas.modern_name: Coarsest (intrinsic) topological stratification and its existence/uniqueness for pseudomanifolds / CS-sets

missed.claim: Grothendieck formulates, apparently independently and possibly before Goresky–MacPherson and King, an intrinsic topological stratification of an arbitrary space via a 'mobility index'. He also asks which spaces admit it, calling them 'presque raisonnables', within his tame-topology programme.
missed.quote: On dit que x a un ordre de mobilité ν si x est ν-mobile mais non (ν+1)-mobile.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is historical priority and context only. The mathematics (intrinsic stratification of CS-sets / pseudomanifolds) is established in the literature. The axiomatic question of which tame ('dévissable') spaces have a well-behaved mobility stratification links to o-minimal topological stratifications, but is largely addressed there.

missed.claim: Conjecture (next page, margin) that Prop B — local product with an immobile normal slice, of locally constant type — holds for all 'dévissable' spaces.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a conjecture for Grothendieck's (never formalized) class of dévissable spaces. It is comparable to known results for definable sets in o-minimal structures, so it is likely subsumed rather than new.

deep.surprise_reason: These are clean, unpublished definitions of a purely topological intrinsic stratification ('immobile singularities', 'order of mobility') inside the tame-topology notes. It is historically interesting, but the notion is standard today: King's and Goresky–MacPherson's intrinsic stratification. No new theorem appears on this page.
transcription_corrections: 'singularité élémentaire {+immobile+} (ou [-...-])': the insertion above reads 'immobile', and the crossed parenthetical is illegible. The later line '(Ainsi les singularités élémentaires, ou immobiles, ...)' confirms 'immobile'.
'de X [-voisins-] non singuliers': the crossed word looks like 'voisins'/'voisinés', uncertain. The final line reads 'le long desquels X est équisingulier'.
'X [-est-] est loc. de dim. finie': the first crossed word may be 'B' or 'Es', not 'est'.
